X identity setup 路 Operator guide

Author rewards v2 and sponsored claims

The primary author-rewards dashboard uses the deployed historical VoxdueRewards contract at 0x4FE62e5e94f3351c9325A1aBad150a1529DfEb6C and the demo tUSD token at 0x96c7aECe3349392a1E51E47D9Ed421e606Bb892f, on chain 46630. It uses the same X OAuth session as the earlier integration but a separate challenge, typed-signature domain, contract and reward numbering. Never reuse authorizations or receipts between versions.

Public /api/v2/stats and /api/v2/rewards are chain reads. Author lookup and claims require the configured X credentials. GET /api/v2/wallet/challenge?rewardId=...&address=... returns a one-use, contract-bound wallet message; POST /api/v2/rewards/:id/claim returns authorization for a wallet-paid transaction. Every POST requires the session CSRF token and exact Origin. POST /api/v2/rewards/:id/relay performs the same verification and optionally broadcasts the transaction from a configured testnet relayer, returning a transaction hash for confirmation.

Relaying is disabled by default. To enable controlled testnet sponsorship after configuring and validating X, explicitly set V2_RELAY_ENABLED=true, supply one of V2_RELAYER_PRIVATE_KEY or V2_RELAYER_KEY_FILE, and fund that relayer with test ETH. The default limits are V2_RELAY_DAILY_BUDGET_ETH=0.0001 and V2_RELAY_MAX_TX_ETH=0.00001. The service reserves a conservative upper gas estimate before broadcasting and persists its budget record under server/.data/. Preserve that file across restarts. Use one process only until locking, distributed queues and shared limits are independently reviewed. The relay key must never enter frontend variables or public hosting.

The user receives the signed creator payout after the 3% claim fee; sponsored gas is a separate operator expense. Funding, token approvals, faucet requests and refunds are not sponsored. If no relayer is configured or its budget is unavailable, the UI provides the wallet-paid claim route. A returned hash indicates submission, not confirmed success.

The V2 EIP-712 domain is the historical Voxdue Rewards, version 2, chain ID 46630, with the v2 address as verifyingContract. The domain remains unchanged for signature compatibility; the presentation brand is Honoro. The type remains Claim(uint256 rewardId,address recipient,uint64 deadline). Any sender may broadcast it, but it always pays the signed recipient. The trusted attestor can authorize payouts and is immutable; disabling the server is not a contract pause.

The original integration instructions below remain applicable to shared credentials and OAuth. Its original /api/rewards routes and Voxdue X Rewards version-1 domain apply only to the preserved older X escrow.

Operator guide 路 Optional integration 路 18 September 2026

The X-author reward studio, OAuth server, and separate X-identity escrow are delivered as code. Real X login is not configured, and no real X account has been authenticated in this delivery. The wallet-directed pilot already works without this service. Do not replace its honest status with a claim of verified social identity until the steps below have been completed.

2. Obtain and configure operator credentials

Register a developer application in the X Developer Console. Enable OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code with PKCE and authorize the intended application type. The implemented scopes are tweet.read users.read; the app does not request permission to post, send DMs, follow accounts, or access email.

For local use, the exact callback is http://127.0.0.1:5177/api/auth/x/callback, subject to X accepting that development callback in the app settings. If the platform requires an HTTPS development origin, use a controlled HTTPS origin and set both the registered callback and PUBLIC_ORIGIN consistently. Do not substitute localhost for 127.0.0.1 without updating both sides.

For the intended public site, the callback would be https://honoro.xyz/api/auth/x/callback only after the domain is registered, configured, and serving the application. Domain and X account ownership are not completed by this repository.

Environment variableRequired value / purpose
PUBLIC_ORIGINExact browser-facing origin; local default http://127.0.0.1:5177. Production must be HTTPS.
X_CLIENT_IDOAuth client ID from the registered X application.
X_CLIENT_SECRETSupply when the chosen confidential-client type requires it.
X_BEARER_TOKENOperator API bearer token with access to post and user lookup; fund the applicable API credit budget.
CLAIM_ATTESTOR_PRIVATE_KEYOne server-only key source matching the deployed immutable attestor. Never expose it in the browser.
CLAIM_ATTESTOR_KEY_FILEAlternative to the direct key variable: an explicit server-only file path. Use one key source, not both.
RH_TESTNET_RPC_URLTrusted RPC for chain 46630; public default is https://rpc.testnet.chain.robinhood.com.
PORTAPI port; default 8787. The server binds to loopback.
NODE_ENVDevelopment locally; production requires HTTPS PUBLIC_ORIGIN.

The existing testnet contract uses the deployment wallet as its immutable attestor. Startup checks that the configured signer matches the deployed address. A different key cannot silently replace it; a future production key arrangement needs a separate reviewed deployment.

Never use a VITE_ environment prefix for an X secret, bearer token, or attestor key: Vite-prefixed values can enter frontend code. Do not paste secrets into documentation, issue reports, chat logs, screenshots, or public deployment JSON.

3. Run the local services

Create the private server configuration from the provided template and edit it locally using the operator's own credentials:

cd server
npm ci
Copy-Item -LiteralPath .env.example -Destination .env
npm start

Do not overwrite an existing configured .env file with the template. The server starts in a disabled state if credentials are absent; that is an expected safe result. Restart the server after changing configuration because readiness is evaluated at startup.

In a separate terminal, run the website:

cd website
npm ci
npm run dev

Open http://127.0.0.1:5177. The Vite /api proxy keeps browser requests on the same origin as the app, while the API process listens on port 8787. The author studio reads /api/health and /x-deployment.json before enabling funding or login.

Readiness checks require configuration, the correct chain, deployed contract code, and a matching attestor address. A true xEnabled response means those checks passed; it does not prove that the bearer token is authorized, API credits are sufficient, or real OAuth has succeeded. Complete the live validation checklist before launch.

4. API contract

EndpointBehavior
GET /api/healthReturns xEnabled, chain ID, and a safe disabled reason when applicable.
GET /api/sessionCreates/reads the browser session; returns the authenticated user or null and a CSRF token.
GET /api/x/post?url=...Validates an allowlisted HTTPS X URL, fetches official post/author data, and returns numeric IDs and display text.
GET /api/auth/x/start?returnTo=...Creates one-time OAuth state and PKCE challenge and redirects to X. Return targets are constrained to the local app.
GET /api/auth/x/callbackValidates state, exchanges the code, retrieves the numeric user ID, rotates the session, and returns to the app.
POST /api/auth/logoutRequires CSRF and matching origin; deletes the session.
GET /api/wallet/challenge?rewardId=...&address=...Requires an authenticated X session and CSRF token; issues a one-time wallet ownership message.
POST /api/rewards/:id/claimVerifies wallet proof, active escrow, OAuth author ID, and a fresh official post lookup; returns recipient, deadline and EIP-712 signature.

The server does not submit the claim transaction or pay its gas. The receiving wallet sends the final contract transaction and pays testnet network gas. A returned claim signature alone does not prove settlement; inspect the confirmed transaction receipt.

5. Security model and data handling

OAuth state lasts ten minutes. The authenticated session lasts one hour and stores only user ID, username and name in memory. The temporary X access token is used for the authenticated identity lookup and is not retained. No refresh-token flow is requested by this pilot.

The wallet challenge lasts five minutes and binds the origin, chain, reward, X ID, wallet address, and nonce. The server consumes it before asynchronous work to prevent concurrent reuse. The attestation is Claim(uint256 rewardId,address recipient,uint64 deadline), under the historical Voxdue X Rewards v1 domain for the exact chain and contract. Its deadline is at most three minutes and always before reward expiry.

The contract itself cannot verify X. It trusts the immutable attestor, which can authorize any active X reward. Correct behavior depends on both secure key custody and correct API/session checks. There is no key rotation or pause in this testnet contract. Expiry refunds remain available to the original payer under their recorded rules; an already misdirected claim cannot be undone by an administrator.

HTTPS sessions use Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookies with the __Host- prefix. The API applies CSRF/origin checks, request-size limits, security headers, no-store caching, and rate limits. Those protections do not make the system production-ready by themselves.

Sessions and rate limits are held in process memory. A restart clears sessions; a multi-instance deployment requires durable shared stores. A production reverse proxy must route /api to the internal server on the same public origin. Review trusted proxy/IP handling before internet exposure so rate limits identify clients correctly. Keep the signing key outside the web root and frontend build.

6. Activation checklist

  • The X application has the exact callback and expected client type.
  • Post and user lookup work using the actual approved API access and funded credits.
  • /api/health reports the correct chain and configured state without exposing secrets.
  • A real X account completes OAuth, and its numeric ID matches /2/users/me.
  • A known public post resolves to its actual numeric author ID.
  • The actual author can sign a wallet challenge and claim a small test reward.
  • A different X account is rejected even if it supplies the author's handle.
  • Wrong wallet signatures, expired/reused challenges, altered rewards and mismatched post authors are rejected.
  • Logout and session expiry behave correctly; application restart has the documented effect.
  • Deleted/private posts, empty API credits, X rate limits, RPC failures and user cancellations fail clearly.
  • An expired unclaimed X reward can be refunded without X login.
  • Privacy copy accurately covers the enabled session cookies and identity processing.
  • Independent review, signer custody and operating controls are completed before any production asset use.

The backend has automated tests using mocked X/chain responses. These are useful security and integration checks, but they do not authenticate a real X account or prove the operator's live credentials work. Treat any synthetic contract smoke signature in the same way: it validates contract mechanics, not the social identity claim.
